This was the strongest non-adjacent candidate, but exact current construction cannot be reproduced from the official FINRA file alone. Replacing missing denominators or universe filters would create a new proxy hypothesis rather than implement the published SII.

The official history is current and the published action is reproducible, but all 49 official observations after the paper sample ended have absolute bullish-minus-bearish spread at or below 30 percentage points. The exact selected rule therefore makes zero independent decisions; reusing 2022-2025 would overlap the selection sample, and relaxing the threshold would create a new searched hypothesis.

The SEC official flattened carrier is current through 2026 Q2, but the primary literature uses multiple standardized transaction/share/value constructions and overlapping 1/3/6/12-month continuous regressions rather than one fixed trade threshold and action. A sign rule would be a new hypothesis, while the repository's post-Unit-112 source screen already rejected Form 4 for horizon and causal-action readiness.

published_construction.ewsi: Equal-weighted mean across eligible firms of short positions divided by shares outstanding, after a price-above-USD-5 filter and a market-capitalization filter above the NYSE fifth percentile.
published_construction.sii: Standardized residual from a linear time-trend regression of log(EWSI).
published_construction.causal_availability: FINRA publishes the twice-monthly security-level position snapshots on the seventh business day after the reporting settlement date.
published_construction.fixed_direction_and_horizon: Higher SII predicts lower next-month aggregate returns in the published mechanism.

published_source.title: Can AAII Beat the Market? A Long-Horizon Backtest of Sentiment-Driven Strategies in E-mini S&P 500
published_source.signal: S equals AAII bullish percentage minus bearish percentage
published_source.fixed_published_action: Long one contract for one week when S is below -30 percentage points, short one contract for one week when S is above +30 percentage points, otherwise flat; enter on the first trading day following publication.
published_source.selection_caveat: The paper evaluated absolute thresholds of 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 percentage points and selected 30 on the full reported sample. It reports no train-test split and no formal data-snooping correction.

official_current_carrier.boundary_rule: Strictly greater than 30 percentage points in absolute spread, matching the paper's S < -tau and S > tau inequalities.

aaii_weekly_sentiment_exactness_audit.causal_timing_note: AAII's current official page says the weekly survey closes Wednesday 23:59 Eastern and results are published Thursday morning, whereas the preprint describes Thursday 16:00 Eastern. A future unit would need to freeze a conservative post-release execution time before reading outcomes; the discrepancy is secondary here because the true post-paper interval contains zero fixed-threshold decisions.
aaii_weekly_sentiment_exactness_audit.adjacency_note: The information source is a Program 2 external sentiment state rather than the pure weekday treatment closed by Lab Unit 111. Its Friday implementation surface would still require an explicit non-calendar causal declaration, but no such unit is opened because the independent decision census is empty.
aaii_weekly_sentiment_exactness_audit.engineering_correction: The official carrier is legacy BIFF XLS. The original bytes remained unchanged; a hidden read-only Excel instance produced a temporary OpenXML copy so the required spreadsheet reader could inspect values. This format bridge is not a research or engineering failure and is not retained as evidence.
aaii_weekly_sentiment_exactness_audit.conclusion: The exact published 30-point AAII rule is currently reproducible but has no independent post-paper decisions. No target economics, Lab unit, optimization campaign or tester path is opened, and no success or failure is declared.
